evidence.note: Claim: a worker that spawns roborev via _spawn(start_new_session=True) orphans the daemon to init when it dies before teardown. Probe: spawned roborev daemon run under a scratch HOME, killed the spawner, daemon survived (os.path.exists(/proc/<pid>) True); with preexec_fn prctl(PR_SET_PDEATHSIG, SIGKILL) it died. CONFIRMED.

Applied rules governing this fix: r-task-phase-needs-wave (fix task is under bugs-2 with wave:0 tag), r-gemini-key-load (GEMINI_API_KEY exported from [REDACTED:path] before review), D-agent-test-etiquette (selected tests only).

tests/test_isolation_roborev_daemon.py: _spawn now arms PR_SET_PDEATHSIG(SIGKILL) via preexec_fn so a daemon dies with its spawner; new regression test test_a_daemon_does_not_outlive_a_spawner_that_dies_without_teardown fails pre-fix (AssertionError: daemon outlived the worker) and passes post-fix (4 passed).

chunk_findings.detail: `_arm_parent_death_signal` is a `preexec_fn` that calls `ctypes.CDLL("libc.so.6")` after fork. CPython documents that `preexec_fn` is not thread-safe: if any other thread holds the allocator or dynamic-linker lock at the moment `_spawn` forks (pytest-cov, timeout plugins, logging threads), the child blocks forever inside `dlopen`/`prctl` and the parent blocks in `Popen` waiting for an exec that never happens. Every caller of `_spawn`, not only the new test, hangs on that input; a raw `prctl` syscall without `dlopen` in the child would not.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_isolation_roborev_daemon.py:45

chunk_findings.detail: Arming `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` without the `getppid()==1` check leaves the orphan the comment claims is impossible. If the worker is killed after `fork` returns in the parent and before `preexec_fn` runs, the child is already reparented to init; `prctl` then succeeds with no pending signal, and the daemon stays up forever. The new test never hits that window: it only `kill()`s the spawner after `_pid_under` sees a pidfile, which is after exec, so it can pass while that start-up race still reproduces B2d2c474d47.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_isolation_roborev_daemon.py:45

chunk_findings.detail: The earlier preexec_fn deadlock still stands. Loading `libc.so.6` at import only removes `dlopen` from the child; `_arm_parent_death_signal` is still a Python `preexec_fn`, and CPython runs it after `fork` in a child that inherits lock ownership. If any other thread holds the GIL (or the allocator) when `_spawn` forks — pytest-cov, timeout plugins, logging — the child blocks forever inside the `prctl`/`getppid` bytecode and the parent blocks in `Popen` waiting for an exec that never happens. Every `_spawn` caller hangs on that input, not only the new test.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_isolation_roborev_daemon.py:40

chunk_findings.detail: The new `getppid() == 1` guard does not close the fork-to-prctl window the comment claims. If the worker is killed after `fork` returns in the parent and before `preexec_fn` runs, the child is already reparented. Under a child subreaper (`PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER`, typical of `systemd --user` and some container/pytest supervisors) the new parent is not pid 1, so the check does not `_exit`, `prctl` arms `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` against a parent that is already dead, and no signal is pending. The daemon then execs and stays up forever — the same orphan as B2d2c474d47. The new test never hits that window: it `kill()`s the spawner only after `_pid_under` sees a pidfile, which is after exec, so it passes even if this check is deleted or wrong.
